A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the DNA-binding domain of the receptor, which is the region most conserved between estrogen receptors and the other members of the steroid receptor superfamily, is a critical determinant in the ability of estrogen receptors to modulate transcription by non-ERs.
ERs are able to modulate the activity of transcription factors that are involved in the regulation of genes that are not regulated by ERs.

ERs potentiate transcription of the collagenase gene by Stat5b and activating protein 1 through a classical mechanism of action and through a non-classical mechanism of action that involves cross-talk between ERs and Stat5b.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DNA binding activity of ERs is not required for the potentiation of Stat-5b transcriptional activity.
the DNA-binding domain of the ER plays a crucial role in the modulation of the activity of other transcription factors.
ERs are not only able to discriminate between agonists and antagonists on a given promoter but also discriminate between different mechanisms of action of the same ligand on different promoters.
